summary: All-electric seaglider for fast coastal passenger transport over water.
editor_note: Regional coastal travel is recast as a vessel that floats, foils, then flies in ground effect: the 12-passenger Viceroy targets 180 mph and 180 miles on existing batteries. Compared to a ferry, it prioritizes speed; unlike an aircraft, it stays over water and uses maritime infrastructure. A human-crewed flight and explicit operating sequence earn the feature, while certification and production remain formidable.

product_evidence.claim: The Viceroy is a 12-passenger all-electric seaglider designed to float, hydrofoil, and then fly in wing-in-ground effect over water.
REGENT states a 180 mph speed and 180-mile range with existing battery technology and has completed a human-crewed flight.

market_context.primary_user: Ferry, airline, logistics, and defense operators serving regional coastal routes.
market_context.differentiation: A maritime-certified craft combines dock access and hydrofoiling with wing-in-ground-effect cruise.
market_context.why_now: Existing batteries can support meaningful coastal range when the craft avoids the energy demands of conventional high-altitude flight.

risks.claim: Certification, passenger operations, and repeatable manufacturing remain much harder than a successful crewed demonstration.
risks.basis: The financing is explicitly directed toward scaling manufacturing after the first human-crewed flight milestone.
